examples.en: That politician made empty promises again.
Promises that are only words easily become empty promises.

examples.ko: 선거 때 한 약속이 공수표로 끝났어요.
examples.en: The promise made during the election ended up being empty.
It's hard to trust someone who only makes lots of empty promises.

examples.ko: 사장님이 월급을 올려 준다고 했는데 공수표였어요.
examples.en: The boss said he'd raise my pay, but it was an empty promise.

examples.ko: 저는 공수표를 던지는 사람이 되고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to be a person who throws out empty promises.

explain: 원래는 돈이 없는 계좌에서 끊은 수표라는 뜻이지만, 요즘은 거의 '지키지 않을 약속'을 비유할 때 써요. 보통 '공수표를 날리다', '공수표로 끝나다'처럼 말해요. 약속을 한 사람을 비판하는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 그 후보는 선거 때마다 공수표를 날려요.
phrases.en: That candidate makes empty promises every election.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지키지 못할 약속을 쉽게 한다는 비판의 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It carries a critical tone, suggesting someone makes promises too easily that they can't keep.

explain_en: It originally means a check drawn on an account with no money, but today it is used almost entirely as a metaphor for a promise that won't be kept. People usually say '공수표를 날리다' or '공수표로 끝나다'. It carries a tone of criticizing the person who made the promise.

examples.ko: 광고주가 새 광고를 마음에 들어 했어요.
examples.en: The advertiser liked the new ad.
The advertiser changed, so the ad content changed too.
The broadcaster is busy looking for advertisers.
The advertiser made many requests, so the work was delayed.
I sent a results report to the advertiser.
YouTubers sign with advertisers and then film videos.

explain: 광고를 만드는 곳은 '광고 회사'이고, 광고비를 내고 맡기는 쪽이 '광고주'예요. '고객'이나 '클라이언트'라고도 하지만 광고 업계에서는 '광고주'가 기본이에요.
explain_en: The company that makes ads is a '광고 회사', and the side that pays and commissions them is the '광고주'. People also say '고객' or '클라이언트', but in the ad industry '광고주' is the standard word.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 모든 물건이 천 원 균일가예요.
examples.en: In this shop, everything is a flat 1,000 won.

examples.ko: 오늘은 모든 티셔츠가 오천 원 균일가로 팔려요.
examples.en: Today all T-shirts are sold at a flat 5,000 won.
I bought cups and plates at a flat-price store.

examples.ko: 균일가 행사 덕분에 돈을 많이 아꼈어요.
examples.en: I saved a lot of money thanks to the flat-price sale.

examples.ko: 균일가라서 크기나 종류 상관없이 같은 값이에요.
examples.en: It's a flat price, so it costs the same regardless of size or type.

examples.ko: 만 원 균일가 코너에는 사람이 정말 많아요.
examples.en: The 10,000-won flat-price corner is really crowded.

explain: '천 원 균일가'처럼 가격 뒤에 붙여서 종류와 상관없이 값이 같다는 뜻을 나타내요. '균일가 매장/행사'로도 많이 써요. 팔다 남은 물건을 싸게 파는 '떨이'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It is attached after a price, as in '천 원 균일가', to mean everything costs the same regardless of type. It is also used in '균일가 매장/행사'. It differs from '떨이', which is selling leftover goods cheaply.

examples.en: The kid next door is so unruly.

examples.ko: 극성스럽게 짖는 강아지 때문에 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep because of a puppy barking wildly.

examples.ko: 그 엄마는 아이 교육에 극성스러운 편이에요.
examples.en: That mother is rather overzealous about her child's education.
The relentless mosquitoes disappeared once autumn came.

examples.ko: 팬들이 극성스러워서 가수가 밖에 나가기 힘들대요.
examples.en: I hear the fans are so intense that the singer finds it hard to go out.
I want to raise a child who isn't too wild.

explain: 지나치게 열성적이거나 유난스러워서 주변이 부담스러울 때 쓰는 말로, 대체로 좋지 않은 뉘앙스예요. 아이 교육에 열심인 부모를 '극성 엄마'라고 부르기도 해요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '극성스러워요, 극성스러운'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It describes someone excessively eager or fussy to the point of being a burden to others, and usually has a negative tone. Parents very intense about their kids' education are sometimes called '극성 엄마'. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective: '극성스러워요, 극성스러운'.

examples.ko: 이 제품은 문제가 있어서 리콜이 결정됐어요.
examples.en: A recall was decided for this product because of a problem.
The car company announced that it will recall the cars.
I saw news about a milk recall on TV.

examples.ko: 리콜 대상인지 번호로 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can check by number whether it is subject to the recall.

examples.ko: 이 모델은 리콜 대상이라서 무료로 수리받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: This model is subject to a recall, so you can get it repaired for free.
The store closed because of the recall.

explain: 리콜은 회사가 결함이 있는 제품을 거두어 고치거나 바꿔 주는 거예요. 손님이 마음에 안 들어서 하는 '환불'이나 '교환'과 달라요. 주로 자동차, 식품, 전자제품 뉴스에서 들어요.
explain_en: 리콜 is when a company takes back a defective product to fix or replace it. It is different from 환불 or 교환, which a customer asks for because they are unhappy with an item. You mostly hear it in news about cars, food, and electronics.

en: pay for; make up for; compensate; recover

examples.ko: 친구 휴대폰을 떨어뜨려서 제가 물어내야 해요.
examples.en: I dropped my friend's phone, so I have to pay for it.
The child who broke the window paid for it.

examples.ko: 빌린 책을 잃어버리면 새 책으로 물어내요.
examples.en: If you lose a borrowed book, you replace it with a new one.
I scratched the rental car, and they told me to pay for the repairs.
I'll make up for what I broke myself.
If you don't want to pay for damage, be careful from the start.

explain: '갚다'는 빌린 것을 돌려줄 때 쓰고, '물어내다'는 내가 망가뜨리거나 손해를 입힌 것의 값을 내놓을 때 써요. 딱딱하게는 '변상하다'라고도 하지만 말할 때는 '물어내다'를 많이 써요. 보통 '~을/를 물어내다' 형태예요.
explain_en: '갚다' is for returning something you borrowed, while '물어내다' is for paying for something you broke or a loss you caused. A formal word is '변상하다', but in speech '물어내다' is common. It is usually used as '~을/를 물어내다'.

examples.en: The size did not fit, so I returned the clothes.
I want to return the shoes I bought online.
I called to return the broken vacuum cleaner.
If you return it within a week, you get your money back.
I gave the box to be returned to the delivery driver.

examples.ko: 포장도 뜯지 않은 물건은 반품할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Items with unopened packaging can be returned.

explain: 산 물건을 판 곳에 돌려보내는 것이에요. 가게에서 직접 바꾸는 건 '교환하다', 돈을 돌려받는 건 '환불하다'라고 해서 구분해요. 보통 '반품하고 환불받다'처럼 이어서 써요.
explain_en: It means sending a purchased item back to the seller. Swapping an item is 교환하다 and getting money back is 환불하다, so the three are distinct. They are often chained, as in 반품하고 환불받다.

examples.en: I'll pay for the cup I broke.
If you break something in a store, you have to pay for it.
I dropped my friend's phone, so I paid for the repair.
The company decided to compensate the customer for the damage.

examples.ko: 수리비가 많이 나와도 변상 범위는 계약서에 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: Even if the repair cost is high, the scope of reimbursement is set in the contract.

examples.ko: 분실물은 변상해 주지 않는 가게도 있어요.
examples.en: Some stores don't pay back for lost items.

explain: 물건을 망가뜨리거나 잃어버렸을 때 돈이나 같은 물건으로 갚는 것에 써요. 일상에서는 '물어 주다'라고도 해요. '배상하다'는 남에게 입힌 손해를 갚는다는 느낌이 강하고, '보상하다'는 손실을 채워 줄 때 써요.
explain_en: It is used when you pay back with money or the same item for something you broke or lost. In daily talk people also say '물어 주다'. '배상하다' strongly means making up for harm done to others, while '보상하다' is for making up for a loss.

examples.en: The company compensated the customer for the loss.
The insurance company covers the repair costs.
I'll make up for the plate I broke.

examples.ko: 늦게 와서 미안하니까 밥으로 보상하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'm sorry I came late, so I want to make it up with a meal.

examples.ko: 사고 피해를 보상하는 방법을 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking into how to compensate for the accident damage.
We have to reward the employees who worked hard.

explain: '보상하다'는 손해나 노력에 대해 돈이나 선물로 갚을 때 써요. '보답하다'는 고마움을 마음이나 행동으로 갚는 느낌이 더 커요. 일상에서는 '갚다', '보답하다'도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: 보상하다 is used for paying back a loss or effort with money or gifts. 보답하다 leans toward repaying kindness with feeling or action. In daily talk, 갚다 and 보답하다 are also common.

en: come thick and fast; rain down; hail down

examples.ko: 방송이 나간 뒤 항의 전화가 빗발쳤어요.
examples.en: After the broadcast, protest calls poured in.

examples.ko: 새 제품에 대한 문의가 빗발치고 있어요.
examples.en: Inquiries about the new product are pouring in.

examples.ko: 사과하라는 요구가 빗발치자 회사가 입장을 밝혔어요.
examples.en: When demands for an apology flooded in, the company stated its position.

examples.ko: 축하 메시지가 빗발쳐서 휴대폰이 계속 울렸어요.
examples.en: Congratulation messages kept pouring in, so my phone kept ringing.

examples.ko: 비난이 빗발치는데도 그는 아무 말도 하지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even as criticism rained down, he said nothing.
What do we do if refund requests come flooding in?

explain: '~이/가 빗발치다' 꼴로 쓰고, 전화, 문의, 항의, 비난, 요청처럼 많은 것이 한꺼번에 몰려올 때 써요. 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 보이고, 좋은 일(축하 메시지)과 나쁜 일(비난) 모두에 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used in the pattern '~이/가 빗발치다' when many things arrive all at once, such as calls, inquiries, complaints, criticism or requests. It often appears in news articles and works for both good things (congratulations) and bad things (criticism).

examples.en: I politely declined the dinner invitation.
I'm busy, so I plan to decline this gathering.

examples.ko: 낯선 사람의 도움을 사절하고 혼자 걸어갔어요.
examples.en: I turned down the stranger's help and walked on alone.
Our company declines all gifts.
I'd like to refuse sales calls.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 계속되는 인터뷰 요청을 모두 사절했대요.
examples.en: They say that actor turned down every interview request.

explain: '거절하다'와 비슷하지만 '사절하다'는 더 정중하고 딱딱해서, 초대나 선물, 제안을 예의 있게 물릴 때 써요. 가게나 아파트 안내문에는 '외상 사절', '방문 판매 사절'처럼 명사 뒤에 '사절'만 붙여서 '받지 않아요'라는 뜻으로 많이 써요. 친구에게는 보통 '거절하다'나 '싫다고 하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is close to '거절하다' but more polite and formal, used for courteously turning down invitations, gifts or offers. On signs in shops and apartment buildings, '사절' is simply attached to a noun, as in '외상 사절' (no credit) or '방문 판매 사절' (no door-to-door sales), meaning 'we do not accept it'. With friends, people usually say '거절하다' or '싫다고 하다'.

examples.en: I explained it to the customer with all my heart.
I prepared this gift with sincere effort, so please accept it.
We will help you with our whole heart.
The doctor treated me with total dedication.

examples.ko: 성심성의껏 노력하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.en: If you try with all your heart, there will be good results.
He took care of his parents with all his heart.

explain: '해 주다', '돕다', '모시다'처럼 남을 위해 하는 행동 앞에 잘 어울려요. '정성껏', '최선을 다해'와 비슷하지만 더 격식 있고 진심을 강조하는 느낌이라 서비스나 인사말에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It fits actions done for others, such as '해 주다', '돕다' and '모시다'. It is close to '정성껏' and '최선을 다해' but more formal and stresses sincerity, so you often hear it in service situations and polite speech.

examples.en: My refrigerator broke down, so I requested after-sales service.
This company's after-sales service is really fast.

examples.ko: 애프터서비스 기간이 일 년이라서 무료로 고쳐 줘요.
examples.en: The after-sales service period is one year, so they repair it for free.
Where is the phone service center?
It was cheap, but the after-sales service is bad, so I regret it.

examples.ko: 애프터서비스는 어떻게 받을 수 있는지 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked how I could get after-sales service.

explain: 일상에서는 'A/S'라고 쓰고 '에이에스'라고 읽는 일이 많아요. 물건을 산 뒤에 고쳐 주거나 점검해 주는 것을 말하고, '서비스'만 말하면 가게에서 공짜로 더 주는 것을 뜻할 때도 있어서 달라요.
explain_en: In daily life people often write 'A/S' and read it as '에이에스'. It refers to repairs or checkups after you buy something. Just saying '서비스' can also mean a free extra given by a shop, so the two are different.

examples.en: The staff member serves customers kindly.

examples.ko: 전화를 응대할 때는 먼저 인사부터 하세요.
examples.en: When you handle a phone call, start with a greeting.

examples.ko: 갑자기 화난 손님을 응대하느라 점심도 못 먹었어요.
examples.en: I was dealing with an angry customer and couldn't even eat lunch.

examples.ko: 신입 사원은 방문객을 응대하는 법부터 배워요.
examples.en: New employees first learn how to receive visitors.
I responded calmly even to the customer who was complaining.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 직원들이 빠르게 응대해서 기다릴 필요가 없어요.
examples.en: The staff here respond quickly, so there is no need to wait.

explain: 손님, 고객, 전화, 민원처럼 찾아오거나 연락한 사람을 맞아서 상대할 때 써요. 가게나 회사 같은 서비스 상황의 말이라서 친구와 대화할 때는 잘 안 써요. 명사 '응대'는 '고객 응대', '전화 응대'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is used when you meet and deal with people who come or contact you, such as customers, callers or complaints. It belongs to service and workplace situations, so you rarely use it with friends. The noun '응대' appears in phrases like '고객 응대' and '전화 응대'.

examples.en: I was busy all day entertaining guests.

examples.ko: 거래처 사람들을 접대해야 해서 오늘 저녁에 약속이 있어요.
examples.en: I have to entertain clients, so I have plans this evening.

examples.ko: 부장님이 손님을 접대하는 자리에 저도 갔어요.
examples.en: I also went to the dinner where our department head was hosting a guest.
We hosted the relatives who came to our house with great care.
I started preparing the food to serve the guests in the morning.
We keep the costs of entertaining at the company in a separate record.

explain: '대접하다'는 가족이나 친구에게도 쓰지만, '접대하다'는 일 때문에 만난 손님이나 거래처를 모실 때 자주 써요. 그래서 회사 이야기에 많이 나와요. '접대비', '접대 자리'처럼 단어를 붙여서도 써요.
explain_en: '대접하다' can be used for family and friends too, but '접대하다' is often used for guests or business partners you meet for work, so it appears a lot in office talk. It also forms words such as '접대비' (entertainment expenses) and '접대 자리' (an entertaining occasion).

examples.en: The person in charge dealt with the problem right away.
The relevant agency decided to act quickly.
I'll handle this matter myself.
Violations are dealt with according to the rules.

examples.ko: 상황에 맞게 조처하지 않으면 피해가 커져요.
examples.en: If you don't respond appropriately to the situation, the damage grows.
The boss ordered us to handle the urgent problems first.

explain: '처리하다'보다 격식 있고, 문제가 생긴 뒤에 대응하거나 수습하는 느낌이에요. 보통 일, 문제, 사건 같은 말이 목적어로 와요. '조치하다'와 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '처리하다', with a feeling of responding to or sorting out a problem after it has arisen. Objects are usually things like a task, problem or incident. It means the same as '조치하다'.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 처사에 많은 사람이 화가 났어요.
examples.en: Many people got angry at the company's handling of it.
Canceling the contract so suddenly is unreasonable treatment.

examples.ko: 부당한 처사를 당하면 신고할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you are treated unfairly, you can report it.

examples.ko: 선생님의 공정한 처사 덕분에 다툼이 끝났어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the teacher's fair handling, the quarrel ended.
This decision is hard to understand.

examples.ko: 그런 처사가 계속되면 손님이 떠날 거예요.
examples.en: If that kind of treatment continues, customers will leave.

explain: 사람이나 기관이 어떤 일을 처리한 방식을 평가할 때 써요. 대부분 '부당한 처사', '너무한 처사'처럼 불만을 나타내는 말과 함께 나와요. 일상 대화보다는 뉴스나 항의하는 글에 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It is used to judge how a person or organization handled something. It mostly appears with words of complaint, like '부당한 처사' or '너무한 처사', and is seen more in the news or complaints than in casual talk.

examples.en: I'm planning to stay at a hotel tonight.
I'd like to change my check-in date. Is that possible?
Breakfast is included during your stay.

examples.ko: 가족과 함께 투숙하려면 방을 두 개 잡아야 해요.
examples.en: If you want to stay together with your family, you need to book two rooms.

examples.ko: 어제 투숙한 방에서 바다가 잘 보였어요.
examples.en: I could see the sea well from the room where I stayed yesterday.

examples.ko: 그 호텔은 외국인도 투숙할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Foreigners can stay at that hotel too.

explain: 일상에서는 '묵다'라고 하고, '투숙'은 호텔이나 여관에서 지낼 때 안내문이나 뉴스에서 많이 써요. 친구 집에서 자는 것에는 쓰지 않아요. 보통 '투숙하다' 모양으로 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk people say '묵다', while '투숙' is used for staying at a hotel or inn, mostly in notices and the news. You would not use it for sleeping at a friend's house. It is usually used in the form '투숙하다'.

examples.en: The customer complained that the food was late.
The residents protest the construction noise.

examples.ko: 잘못된 판정에 선수들이 항의하는 모습이 보였어요.
examples.en: Players could be seen protesting the wrong call.
I'm thinking of going there and complaining in person.
It seems like protesting won't help.
I was angry and ended up complaining by phone.

explain: 항의하다는 잘못이라고 생각하는 일에 대해 강하게 문제를 제기하는 거예요. '불평하다'는 마음에 안 드는 것을 투덜대는 정도이고, 항의하다는 상대에게 직접 따지는 느낌이 있어요. '~에 항의하다'처럼 이유를 '에'로 말해요.
explain_en: 항의하다 is to strongly raise an objection about something you think is wrong. '불평하다' is grumbling about something you dislike, while 항의하다 means confronting the other party directly. The reason takes 에: '~에 항의하다'.
